rule: mixed: the rule fires, but the producing has no producer — the lantern appears only in the condition, and the two events are joined by nothing more than temporal overlap — and the verb "lighting" reduces to the same symbol `light` that "mist-light" inherits as its head noun, so a mist-light reads as a lighting event. Rewrite as "When a lantern is kindled, the lantern produces mist-light.": a finite condition clause with an explicit subject gives the producing an agent, and it takes the verb off the colliding symbol.
texts: good. fires once per burning occurrence, with the lantern, the mire-essence, the producing and the mist-light all covered.

mixed: no content is lost, but the giving is keyed to the lantern rather than to each burning and carries no link back to it, so a lantern that burns mire-essence twice still yields a single, untimed giving. Rewrite as "When a lantern burns mire-essence, the lantern gives mist-light." — the "when" wording routes to the per-occurrence form your parallel sentence already gets.
good. records mist-light as a kind of flame and a kind of light, keeping both colour words; there is no rule to fire here.
good. the denial distributes to every ordinary oil as a fireable rule at strength 0, and "ordinary" restricts which oil is meant rather than being asserted of oil at large.
